headline.label: Balance owing for 2026 (negative = refund), Ontario resident

steps: Employee CPP: base 4.95% and first additional 1% of earnings between CAD 3,500.00 and YMPE CAD 74,600.00 = CAD 3,519.45 + CAD 711.00; CPP2 4% up to YAMPE CAD 85,000.00 = CAD 416.00; EI 1.63% up to CAD 68,900.00 = CAD 1,123.07 (deducted from pay)
Line 22215 deduction (first additional + CPP2) = CAD 1,127.00; credit amounts: base CPP CAD 3,519.45 (line 30800), EI CAD 1,123.07 (line 31200)
Total income CAD 90,000.00 less RRSP CAD 5,000.00 less CPP deduction CAD 1,127.00 = net income CAD 83,873.00 = taxable income (no other deductions)
Federal tax on CAD 83,873.00 at the 2026 brackets (top dollar at 20.5%) = CAD 13,389.97
Federal credits = (BPA CAD 16,452.00 + CPP/EI CAD 4,642.52 + Canada employment amount CAD 1,501.00) x 14% = CAD 3,163.37; basic federal tax CAD 10,226.60
Ontario tax on CAD 83,873.00 at the 2026 brackets = CAD 5,464.85; credits (BPA CAD 12,989.00 + CPP/EI CAD 4,642.52) x 5.05% = CAD 890.39; basic Ontario tax CAD 4,574.46
Ontario surtax CAD 0.00; tax reduction CAD 0.00; LIFT credit CAD 0.00; Health Premium on taxable income CAD 750.00
Ontario tax = CAD 5,324.46; total income tax = CAD 15,551.06
Less tax already paid CAD 18,000.00 = refund CAD 2,448.94
CAD 1,000.00 more RRSP deduction would save CAD 296.50 of income tax (federal alone: CAD 0.205 per dollar at this income)

expected.why: A Quebec resident files a separate Quebec return (TP-1) with its own taxable income (worker deduction, line 248 QPP and QPIP deduction), pays QPP and QPIP instead of CPP and part of EI, owes the health services fund contribution and the drug insurance premium on the TP-1, and takes the 16.5% Quebec abatement on federal tax. qc-individual-return says the 2026 line 248 factors are not published and the 2025 ones must not be used for 2026; this engine computes none of the Quebec return.

province.description: province of residence on 31 December, two-letter code (QC is refused: Quebec tax is on a separate TP-1 return)

employment_income.description: CAD, T4 employment income from one employer for the whole year (CPP and EI are computed from it)

self_employment_net_income.description: CAD, net self-employment profit (T2125); a loss is not supported

other_income.description: CAD, other fully taxable income with no credit of its own (interest, net rent)

eligible_dividends.description: CAD, actual eligible dividends received (refused if more than 0)

other_dividends.description: CAD, actual other-than-eligible dividends received (refused if more than 0)

rrsp_deduction.description: CAD, RRSP deduction claimed for the year (within the limit on the notice of assessment)

tax_withheld.description: CAD, income tax already deducted at source (T4 box 22) plus instalments paid for the year

has_spouse_or_partner.description: had a spouse or common-law partner on 31 December (refused if true: spouse credits and family tests are not computed)

age_65_or_over.description: 65 or older on 31 December (refused if true: age and pension credits are not computed)

tax_year.description: the tax year the question is about. This engine has figures for 2025 and 2026 only; any other year is refused
